Lemma 9.79 (Cancellation of the finite-fibre discriminant). Let R be a discrete valuation ring containing ℚ. Suppose a key tuple of g sections over R has finite common-zero support on the closed fibre, and its generic fibre has the split transverse data defining (C.63). Then its generic key invariant is a unit after an injective local extension of discrete valuation rings. In particular any nonzero integral power of that invariant lying in R is a unit in R.

Lemma 9.80 (Generic degree-n sections meet transversally). Let k ↪→ K be an extension of fields with K algebraically closed, let x be a key object of dimension g over k with base change x^{′} to K, and let n ≥4. Let b_{1}, . . . , b_{N} (N = n^{g}) be a k-basis of H^{0}(A, L^{n}) pulling back to b^{′}_{1}, . . . , b_{N}^{′} on A_{K}. If the gN coefficients T = (T_{i,j}) ∈K^{g×N} are algebraically independent over k, then the sections s_{i} =∑^{N}_{j=1}T_{i,j}b^{′}_{j}∈ H^{0}(A_{K}, L_{K}^{n}) (1 ≤i ≤g) have finitely many common zeros in A_{K}(K), all with nonzero Lie-basis Jacobian.
